theorem_title: A uniform margin for weighted reciprocal sums
natural_language_statement:
Let $m$ be a natural number, $\Lambda,\epsilon>0$ real numbers, and $S\ge0$ a real number. There exists $X\ge1$ such that, for every real $w_\star>X$ and every real family $(w_i)_{0\le i<m}$ with $w_i\ge w_\star$ for all $i$,

$$\Lambda\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac1{w_i}+\frac S{w_\star}<\epsilon.$$

The same threshold applies to every family with the stated common lower bound, including the empty family when $m=0$.
explanation: Set $X=\max\{1,(\Lambda m+S)/\epsilon\}$. For $w_\star>X$, one has $w_\star>0$ and $\Lambda m+S<\epsilon w_\star$, hence $(\Lambda m+S)/w_\star<\epsilon$. Every $w_i\ge w_\star$ is positive and satisfies $1/w_i\le1/w_\star$. Summing these inequalities and multiplying by $\Lambda>0$ bounds the required expression by $(\Lambda m+S)/w_\star$, proving the strict margin.
